cover.alt: Terminal output of a real killit session: killit inspect 5150 reports a node server as SAFE, ki 5150 5151 5152 kills two node servers and a Python server, and killit 5000 refuses to touch macOS ControlCenter with a warning and exit code 2

gallery.alt: Terminal output of killit inspect 5150 listing port, PID, name, command, path, owner, protocol, project type node and safety SAFE, then killit 5150 printing Killed node, then a second run printing Nothing listening on specified port(s) and exit 0
gallery.caption: killit inspect shows what holds a port: the PID, the command, the owner, a guess at the project type, and a safety level with its reason. A SAFE process stops with a plain killit 5150. Running it again exits 0, because an empty port is not an error.

gallery.alt: Terminal output of killit kill 5150 5151 5152 --dry-run listing three processes it would kill, then ki 5150 5151 5152 printing Killed for two node processes and one Python process
gallery.caption: Several ports go in one command. --dry-run lists what would be killed without sending a signal. The short alias ki then stops two Node servers and a Python http.server.

gallery.alt: Terminal output of killit inspect 5000 showing macOS ControlCenter with safety WARN because its binary is in a system directory, then killit 5000 refusing with a warning and exit 2
gallery.caption: macOS ControlCenter holds port 5000. Its binary lives under /System, so killit classes it WARN and refuses to kill it without --force. The exit code is 2, so scripts can tell a refusal from a success.

gallery.alt: Terminal output: killit 5160 kills a node process, killit inspect 5160 then shows a new node process with a different PID on the same port, killit 5160 --tree kills it, and inspect reports Nothing listening on this port
gallery.caption: The server on port 5160 runs under a small watcher script that restarts it, like nodemon. A plain kill frees the port only until the watcher starts a new process. --tree signals the whole process group, watcher included, so the port stays free.
